description.narrative:
he project will contribute to more sustainable and climate-resilient livelihoods for Salween-basin riverine communities in Myanmar by strengthening inclusive, community-driven water-resource governance and climate resilience practices. This objective aligns with the broader Mekong Inclusion Program aim of “more sustainable and resilient livelihoods of riparian communities, including strengthened women’s leadership, in the Mekong sub-region.” In addition, awareness and knowledge regarding local water governance and climateresilience in Myanmar will increase among both local and international stakeholders, effectively linking Myanmar issues to broader regional dialogues and fostering transboundary understanding and cooperation.
Project Objectives (Pillars): Objective 1: GEDSI and Feminist Influencing: Enhance the leadership roles and active participation of women and marginalized groups in community-based water resource governance structures.
Objective 2: Inclusive Water Resource Governance: Strengthen community-based institutions and civil society networks to effectively manage local water resources inclusively and sustainably.
Objective 3: Climate Resilient Communities: Increase resilience of targeted riverine communities to climate and human-induced changes through locally appropriate adaptation measures.
1.4.2 Results (outputs and outcomes) Pillar 1: GEDSI and Feminist Influencing Outcome 1.1: More women and diverse community leaders, including marginalised social groups actively engaging in WRG and climate related public events, platforms and fora at local, national and regional levels • Output 1.1.1: Community governance structures strengthened with at least 50% women and diverse representation. • Output 1.1.2: Capacity-building trainings delivered to enhance leadership, and networking skills among women and marginalized group leaders.
Outcome 1.2: Increased leadership capabilities and opportunity for women and diverse community members (including marginalised social groups andPWDs) supported by the Project • Output 1.2.1: Tailored mentoring, peer‑learning, and coaching delivered to women and marginalized leaders. • Output 1.2.2: Number of women-led actions and cross-learnings for women and diverse community members includingPWDs supported for inclusive water governance. Pillar 2: Inclusive Water Resource Governance Outcome2.1: Increased awareness of the impact of large-scale river infrastructure, resource use and disasters/climate change among the targeted communities andCSOs • Output 2.1.1: Regular training sessions conducted to build practical water governance and monitoring skills among targeted CSOs and community groups. • Output 2.1.2: Established mechanisms for regular community-led monitoring and resource management practices.
Outcome 2.2: Targeted CSOs, CSO networks and community leaders with increased ability to represent the interests/demands of riverine communities. • Output 2.2.1: Number of CSOs supported (disaggregated by type of organisation) includingfunding and technical support. • Output 2.2.2 : cases supported to CSOs, CSOs networks and community leaders to engage and influence to non-stater actors/ local duty bearers for inclusive water governance practices and policies
Pillar 3: Climate Resilient Communities Outcome 3.1: Targeted riverine communities have increased knowledge of and taking action on local climate and disaster risks mitigation and adaptation. • Output 3.1.1: Community climate risk assessments and action plans developed andendorsed by targeted communities.
Outcome 3.2: Targeted riverine community water resource and disaster risk management structures more inclusive of diverse community members (women, People with disability, Indigenous People and other marginalized socialgroups). • Output 3.2.1: Early warningand preparedness systems established, incorporating indigenous and community-based knowledge.
Outcome 3.3: Targeted riverine households adopting disaster/climate resilient livelihood practices and/or behaviours. •Output 3.3.1: Riverine communities supported to undertake disaster/climate analysis • Output 3.3.2: Families supported to pilot climate resilient livelihoods 1.5 How you want to achieve this: intervention strategy The IP3 intervention strategy inMyanmar emphasizes strengthening community institutions for inclusive water governance and climate resilience. Building upon successful community-based water governance (CBWG) examples from IP-2, community groups will be empowered to sustainably managelocalresources through activities such as regular monitoring, patrolling, and environmental assessments. Climate risk and vulnerability assessments will identify specific risks and inform tailored resilience plans. Communities will demonstrate climate resiliencepractices, including indigenous methods, to increase local awareness and influence policy discussions with local and international stakeholders. Promotion of women’s leadership remains a central, cross-cutting approach, aiming to increase recognitionof women’s vital roles in water governance. Activities will specifically support women's capacity-building and leadership promotion, enhancing community recognition of women's contributions. Disability inclusion will also receive greater focus, partnering withtechnical organizations to raise awareness among CSOs and community focal points. Community dialogues and success stories will highlight effective GEDSI and feminist leadership examples. The strategy includes strengthening civil society organization (CSO)networks and enhancing their capacity for effective advocacy with local authorities. Organizational development and thematic training will support CSOs in facilitating basin-wide coordination and influencing inclusive local water governancepolicies, particularly in progressive areas like Karen State under the KNU governance, and at the village level in Shan State. Documentation, community-based research, and awareness-raising activities will generate evidence to influence regional and international policy discussions, promoting greater awareness of the Salween Basin's challenges and the successes of Myanmar's community-driven approaches.
1.5.2 Activities
Pillar 1: GEDSI and Feminist Influencing OiM will commence with an inception kick-offworkshopinvolving all project partners to introduce the project design, grant processes, compliance requirements, and establish clear working protocols. Additionally, a GEDSI Assessment and Design Workshop will be held in the first year, leveraginglessons fromIP-2, enabling partners to collaboratively design effective GEDSI integration strategies. Over subsequent years (2-4), OiM will facilitate dialogues on women leadership and disability inclusion, empowering marginalized groups by elevating existingwomenleaders' visibility and influence within communities. In Year 4, successful narratives around GEDSI inclusion and feminist leadership in water governance will be documented and disseminated by OiM for broader awareness-raising.
One regionalpartner will directly implement community-focused initiatives across Karen state, incorporating GEDSI as a cross-cutting theme to bolster youth participation, women's leadership, and the inclusion of marginalized groups within community-based water governance (CBWG)structures and civil society networks over years 2-5. Similarly, KTHM and Shwe Inn Thu (SIT) will implement integrated GEDSI activities in Shan state from years 1-4, emphasizing the development of women focal points to enhance women's leadershiproles andinclusionin water resource governance.
Pillar 2: Inclusive WaterResource Governance OiM will support partners and civil society networks, such as SSN, through coordinated advocacy activities and networking at both national and regionallevels (years2-5).In collaboration with academic partners such as Chaing Maing University (CMU), OiM will undertake research and documentation of community-based water governance models employing methodologies like People’s Environmental Impact Assessment(EIA)and FeministParticipatory Action Research (FPAR), disseminating findings through public awareness initiatives (years 3-4). A regional partner will strengthen CBWG committees and lake conservation groups in Karen state, promotingyouth environmentaleducation, community advocacy, and engagement with local and international stakeholders informed by robust research and documentation efforts (years 2-5). Concurrently, KTHM will directly strengthen community structures in Shan state, focusing oncommunity-driven resource management practices, conservation regulations, and advocacy mechanisms from years 2-5.
Pillar 3: Climate Resilient Communities OiM will support climate risk and vulnerability assessments in target communities during years 2-3,facilitating the development oftailored preparedness and resilience-building action plans. Learning exchanges highlighting effective climateresilience models will be convened in years 4-5 to facilitate knowledge sharing among communities and CSOs. Underthegrant provisions, the regional partner will assist CBWG groups in developing comprehensive Climate Resilience Action Plans, providing essential training, skill-building activities, and targeted livelihood support (years 2-5). Likewise, KTHM willenhance adaptive capacities ofwomenand community leaders through tailored resilience training and livelihood interventions in alignment with their climate resilience action plans (years 2-5). SIT, as a new partner, will specifically scale-up community-drivenclimateresilience strategies inShan state's Inle Lake area, commencing implementation from years 1-4. SIT, as a new partner focusing on Shan state's Inle Lake area, will commence in Year 1 with project orientation and inception workshops and will alsoundertake climate risk mapping and planning to identify clear climate actions with communities. In Year 2, SIT will start climate-smart agriculture and GAP training, and climate smart farming pilot initiatives. Community focal persons targeted capacitystrengthening will be the key approach forcascading climate smartpractices and initiatives. In addition, Environmental Conservation Awareness Training, establishing community nurseries for tree planting on World Environment Day, celebrate World Water Daywill be implemented for raising communityawareness. Year 3 will focus onagricultural input provision, scaling up climate smart farming initiatives, and resource management skill-building, alongside continuing tree nursery activities. Year 4 will consolidatelearning and documentations throughfacilitating knowledge and experiences exchanges and maintain community-driven environmental actions through continuous interventions on climate and environment management initiatives.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam great Britain is managing Oxfam in Myanmar. It has an office in Yangon since 2009 and operates in 5 townships as stipulated in its MOU with the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation.
Oxfam’s vision for Myanmar is for all citizens, including women and ethnic nationalities, to be able to enjoy their social, cultural, economic, civil and political rights. We believe it is possible for Myanmar to be led by a government that is responsive and accountable to its citizens; to have a political system everyone can be part of and have a dynamic private sector which works in the interests of the poorest. The focus of our work is now:
Empowering communities to exercise their own rights and increase their influence on local policies and resource allocation; promoting an accountable civil society which is able to drive pro-poor policies and equitable change. Building a responsive local government which can respond to the priorities of its people, engaging networks of communities, civil society and local government in order to work with a widerange of national and international actors. Increasing the participation of women in society, helping them to gain positions of leadership and to participate in decision making processes at all levels. Working towards a pro-poor private sector to ensure the private sector and the government adopt business practices and policies which benefit poor and vulnerable people.
To achieve our goals, the Oxfam Country strategy focuses on three thematic areas of work: Governance and Social Accountability, Economic Justice, and Humanitarian. Gender Equality is a core element in all programs, ensuring that we put women at the centre of everything we do.
